SeaWorld sent animal care and veterinary staff experienced with walruses to Alaska to help provide care for Annautaq, and to help the calf prepare for his 4,000-mile journey to Florida, where he would become one of 43,000 orphaned, injured, rejected, or otherwise needy animals since its establishment.

In part, it was because the US Fish and Wildlife Service determined he could not be released back into the wild. Pacific walruses rely solely on their mothers’ milk for nutrition throughout their first year of life and depend on their mother for protection and the development of essential survival and social behaviors.

With his mother out of the picture, his placement at SeaWorld Orlando was guided by long-term care and social needs, including the opportunity to grow up alongside other walruses, 3 others being housed at the center.

“Annautaq’s story shows why having specialized marine mammal rehabilitation capacity in Alaska is so important,” said Jane Belovarac, wildlife response curator at the Alaska SeaLife Center. “Getting Annautaq to this point took an incredible network of people, and we’re proud the ASLC could provide the specialized care that helped carry him from rescue in Alaska to his next chapter.”

RESCUING MARINE LIFE:

At SeaWorld Orlando, Annautaq is receiving up to 6 bottle feedings a day, veterinary care and 24-hour support during a planned 30-day quarantine to help protect the health of the resident animals.

“As he settles in, we’ll make introductions to Garfield, Kaboodle and Uki at his pace,” said Jim Kinsler, curator at SeaWorld Orlando. “Kaboodle’s experience caring for rescued calves and the opportunity to connect with 2-year-old Uki, herself a rescued walrus, make this herd a promising setting for him to learn, build relationships and grow.”

As he acclimates, Annautaq will join Uki in playing an essential role as an ambassador for their species, educating the public on the challenges Pacific walruses face in the wild. His story, like those of many other animals rescued by SeaWorld Orlando, emphasizes the park’s ongoing mission to inspire action toward the protection and preservation of marine life.

Talk about beyond the pale!

New Jersey's notorious "Tan Mom" claims federal immigration agents nearly slapped her in handcuffs after questioning her American citizenship, allegedly because of the famously deep tan that made her a tabloid sensation.

Patricia Krentcil recounted the bizarre encounter during an appearance on the "Light. Tan. Up." podcast alongside actor Tom Arnold, claiming U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents stopped her as she left a restaurant with girlfriends.

CONTROVERSIAL ICE TACTIC ACTUALLY REDUCES UNINTENDED 'COLLATERAL' ARRESTS: FEDERAL AGENT

Patricia Krentcil, better known as "Tan Mom," claims ICE agents questioned her U.S. citizenship because of her dark tan during an appearance on the "Light. Tan. Up." podcast. (Light. Tan. Up. with Tan Mom & Adam Barta)

"As we're walking out, the ICE people stopped me and they asked me, 'Am I an American citizen?'" Krentcil recalled. "And I'm like, 'Yes.' You know, like it blew my mind."

But according to the longtime bronzing enthusiast, the encounter nearly took a turn even darker than her tan.

"Because I was so tan, they were about to handcuff me ... and take me away. God knows where," she alleged.

Krentcil, whose unusually bronzed complexion has attracted national attention for more than a decade, claimed she feared being detained and transported to an unknown location.

DHS CONDEMNS ROSIE O’DONNELL AFTER ‘DISGUSTING’ CLAIM THAT DETAINED IMMIGRANTS ARE RAPED IN ICE FACILITIES

An exterior view of a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) administrative office and processing center on June 28, 2025. (Paul Weaver/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

"Once you get in those trucks, you don't know where you're going anymore," she said. "I was scared, but I held my own and I got out of the situation."

The tanning enthusiast also accused immigration authorities of discriminatory behavior, saying, "But they're very racist about color and nationalities and stuff like that."

DHS FIRES BACK AT PARAMORE'S HAYLEY WILLIAMS AFTER ‘F--- ICE' CONCERT OUTBURST

Krentcil rose to notoriety in the 2010s for her trademark deep bronzed tan. (iStock)

She also described the alleged ordeal as "terrifying."

Krentcil did not specify when or where the encounter allegedly occurred, and Fox News Digital has not independently verified her account.

Krentcil first shot to national notoriety in 2012 after authorities accused her of bringing her then-5-year-old daughter into a tanning bed at a New Jersey salon.

She was arrested and charged with second-degree child endangerment after her daughter reportedly arrived at school with sunburns, sparking a media frenzy over Krentcil's extreme tanning habits and parenting.

The case ultimately ended without an indictment. An Essex County grand jury declined to indict Krentcil in February 2013, and the charges were dropped.

Krentcil has since traded New Jersey for Florida, where the woman whose famously deep tan made her a tabloid sensation continues to embrace life in the Sunshine State.
